newsitem.title: ITALY: Benetton upbeat on 1997, expansive in U.S.
newsitem.headline: Benetton upbeat on 1997, expansive in U.S.

text.p: Italian clothing company Benetton Group SpA could open new megastores as part of a plan to boost its presence in the United States, Benetton managing director Carlo Gilardi said on Friday.
Gilardi, interviewed on Reuters Financial Television, was also upbeat on prospects for 1997, saying the year had started fairly well although it was too early to give any figures.

"I think 1997 will give us good satisfaction in terms of sales and net profit. In any case we feel confident that the result of 1997 will be more or less in line with 1996 and may be more," he said in the interview.
He said the group was maintaining its market quota in the United States taking into account strong competition there.
"But in any case we have some plans there that unfortunately right now I can't disclose," he said.

"But don't forget that in 1996 we opened one of the most exciting megastores of the world in Fifth Avenue. So the idea is maybe to speed up the megastores a bit and maybe include some other megastores in the States as we did in New York," he said.
Benetton announced on Thursday that 1996 net profits rose 11.5 percent from 1995 levels and pushed up its dividend 18 percent to 500 lire per share.
It also said it had a 133 billion lire cash pile which has prompted speculation as whether it will make an acquisition.
Gilardi said: "The normal attitude of any company is to look around to see if there are acquisitions to be done."

"It's very difficult to find the right thing to buy first of all because we don't want to diversify the business. We want to continue in our apparel investment and maybe speed up some other brand that we have in our portfolio," he said.
Another alternative could be to make an acquisition "that fits in well with our philosophy and our strategy on the commercial side and the production side," he added.
He also noted the group intended to pay a higher dividend to satisfy minority shareholders in particular and also planned to invest in its production cycle by improving technology.
But he added: "This will not imply a large investment because we made large investment a few years ago."
